timothy1.3.p1.b1.text: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.

timothy1.3.p1.b2.text: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, … hospitable, able to teach,

timothy1.3.p1.b3.text: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.

timothy1.3.p1.b4.text: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?

timothy1.3.p2.b1.text: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited …

timothy1.3.p2.b2.text: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, …

timothy1.3.p2.b3.text: Deacons likewise must be dignified, … They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.

timothy1.3.p2.b4.text: Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.

timothy1.3.p3.b1.text: In the same way, the women must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.

timothy1.3.p3.b2.text: Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things

timothy1.3.p3.b3.text: in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s household,

timothy1.3.p3.b4.text: which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

timothy1.3.p4.b1.text: By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great:

timothy1.3.p4.b2.text: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels,

timothy1.3.p4.b3.text: was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.
